inputs.original_text: This is being dressed up as political change, but it looks more like a managed takeover. If residents are too poor to reclaim what still works, that leaves the door open for wealthy diaspora and foreign investors to buy up property and businesses cheaply. That doesn’t feel accidental: the people who live there could be pushed aside while those with money reap the benefits. The key question is who is shaping this transition—and who stands to profit from it.
inputs.modified_text: This isn’t a genuine political transition—it looks like a takeover designed to make local people too poor to hold on to what still works. Once they’re pushed out of the way, wealthy diaspora and foreign investors can scoop up property and businesses cheaply. The real question is who’s steering this process and arranging things so they profit while residents lose out. I don’t believe that outcome is accidental.
